chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated from Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadqah from the Truth-teller, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his ancestors (peace be upon them) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A prayer in my mosque is equal in the sight of Allah to ten thousand prayers in other mosques, except for the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram), for indeed a prayer in it is equal to one hundred thousand prayers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward multiplier for prayer in Masjid al-Nabawi compared to other mosques?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* establishes the superior spiritual merit of Masjid al-Nabawi, positioning it second only to Masjid al-Haram in the hierarchy of sacred spaces. The specific multiplier of ten thousand highlights the unique status of the Prophet’s burial place as a locus of divine proximity, while the exception for Mecca underscores the absolute preeminence of the Kaaba. This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interconnection between the physical sanctity of the Imams' resting places and the spiritual rewards of worship.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his ancestors that the Holy Prophet (sw) said, “

The reward of offering a Prayer  in  Masjidun  Nabawi  is  equal  to  the  reward  of  ten thousand  Prayers  offered in  any  other  mosque  except  the Prayer offered in Masjidul Haraam whose reward is equal to the reward of a hundred thousand Prayers offered in another mosque.”
